I really, really think I would remember sleeping with you.
Come on, come on. Search your brain, all right? It was...
...a certain amount of time ago. I was here. You were here.
We had sex here, here, here...
Not there.
Anything? - No, it's not ringing any bells.
My God, woman!
How many people have you been with not to remember this?
Hey, Hayley. We really gotta fix that doorknob.
Joey?
I slept with you!
And you obviously remember me! Hey, I still got it!
So we're good.
I'll let myself out.
And I said, "Okay, Vikram...
...you can't just call every time you get lonely.
You gave up that right when you slept with Rachel."
Rachel? I thought she just had a baby with Ross.
Yeah, well...
Yeah.

I know. But he calls, and my heart goes to him.
You know, that bastard is one smooth-talking freelance kite designer.

I mean, you know, I'm... I'm not saying me, but...

And you don't have to worry about glue-sniffing with me.
Although, I do smell the occasional Magic Marker.

Well...

Hi.

questions.en:
Hello.
Hello.
I love my new job!
Honey, you're screaming. - You bet your ass I am.
I just had the best first day ever.
The kitchen? Twice as big as Allessandro's.
Oh, that's great. - Yeah.
And clean? Not just Health Department-clean, Monica-clean.
Awesome.
Oh, and the people are so nice.
There's this one guy, Jeffrey, he's the maitred.
Chandler, you will love him.
He is without a doubt the funniest guy I have ever met.
This is nice. - I know.
You need both hands for that? - Yeah, I kind of do.
Well, how's this?
Oh, look at you two holding hands.
Is this getting serious?
Well, I, you know...
Have you not talked about it yet?
Am I making you uncomfortable?
If you were bigger you'd hit me, huh?
I'm sorry, heh.
It's obviously way too early for us to be having that conversation.
Is it? - Maybe not. Is it?
Okay, when I got divorced...
I didn't think I'd feel this way about someone for a really long time.
Then again, I didn't think I'd meet someone like you.
And this may be crazy-soon, but I want you to have this.
No, not... That's gum. - Oh.
Oh, five bucks. I love it when that happens, you know?
You don't know it's there... - I know. Keep digging.
Oh, sorry.
Oh. It's a key.
To be honest, I think I'd prefer the five dollars.
It's to my apartment. - Oh, wow.
Ooh. Big step for Phoebe and Mike.
Look, I don't want you to feel like you have to give me your key...
No, I want to. - Oh, thank God.
Yeah.
Wow. I was starting to think I'd never meet someone that...
you know, I wanted to do this with.
Here you go.
This is cool, huh? - It really is.
Oh, I know it. It is amazing. These little things open doors.
So I don't go back to work for another four weeks...
but we would like our nanny to start right away...
so that Emma could get a chance to know her.
I think that's really smart.
The easier we can make the transition for her the better.
That's great. Great.
So do you have any questions for us? - Not really.
All right. Well, thank you so much for coming.
Thank you. - It was really nice to meet you.
We will call you. - Oh, you know, wait.
I do have one question. - Yeah.
Do you guys do random drug testing?
Boy, we, uh, hadn't really thought of that.
That's cool. But if you do, I'm gonna need three days' notice.
Okey-dokey.
Wow. We're never gonna find a nanny.
Come on, Rach. We will. I promise. We have more interviews.
And worse comes to worst, we can always reconsider the, uh, first one we met with.
What, the blond with no bra?
She was blond?
Just a sec.
Okay, this one's name is Sandy. - Okay.
She's got a degree in Early Childhood Education.
Uh, she worked for her last family for three years.
Okay.
Hi. I'm Sandy.
And she's a little mannish.
Ah! Oh, my God. David. - Hi.
Uh, is this a bad time? - No, it's a great time. Come in.
Wow. Hi.
Oh, my gosh. What are you doing here? Are you back from Minsk?
Well, just for a couple of days.
I'm here to explain to the people who gave us our grant...
why it's a positive thing that we've spent all their money...
and, uh, accomplished, uh, nothing.
Who cares? It got you here.
Well, it got me to New York anyway. Then I got in a cab at the airport...
and the guy said, "Where to?"
I just gave him your address. I didn't even think about it.
Wow. Where's your luggage?
Damn it.
All right, I'll call the cab company.
We can call them later. Can you just stand there for a moment?
Boy.
There's an old Russian expression, um, that goes
Roughly translated, that means, um
"This thing that I'm looking at: Wow."
Thank you.
Uh, no, you should see me when... Actually, no, I look pretty good.
Are you kidding?
You know, when you don't see someone for a long time...
and you kind of build them up in your head, you start thinking
"Come on, don't be crazy, nobody's that beautiful."
But, well, you are.
Well, so, um, are you seeing anyone?
No.
I'm just the worst person ever.
How can I not tell David that I'm seeing Mike?
Maybe he didn't give you a chance.
He said, "Are you seeing someone?" And I said, "No."
Oh, well, that would've been your window. - Yeah.
I mean, I don't know. I was looking in his eyes...
and I was just thinking, "Oh, my God, it's David. David's here."
He's just so irresistible.
Really? The scientist guy? - Really? Chandler?
Continue.
Okay, then it gets worse...
because I told him I would see him tomorrow night.
Phoebe. - I know. Evil.
And, and, and, and...
I like Mike so much, you know? It's just going really well. Oh, my God.
Wow, isn't it ironic that David would show up...
on the same day that you and Mike exchange keys?
Uh-huh.
Yeah. You know, and given my lifelong search for irony...
you can imagine how happy I am.
What are you gonna do? - I mean, I guess I just have to...
tell David that nothing can happen between us.
Unless I don't.
You know, complicated moral situation?
No right, no wrong? - You have to tell David.
I knew I should've had this conversation with Joey.
Funniest guy she's ever met.
I'm funny, right?
What do you know? You're a door.
You just like knock-knock jokes.
Save it for inside.
Hey. - Hey.
So Oklahoma's a crazy place. You know, they call it the Sooner State.
Frankly, I'd sooner be in any other state.
And what's with Oklahoma having a panhandle?
Can all states have stuff like that?
Hey, yeah, I'm from the, uh, waistband of Wyoming.
But when I was 7, we headed over to the crotch.
Was your cabin pressurized?
And don't get me started on the way the people from Tulsa talk.
Okay.
What's with the word "y'all"?
You know, just two words just pushed together?
Are we all allowed to do that? Because if so, I say why stop there?
You know, your new poodle could be your noodle.
And fried chicken could be fricken.
Waiter? Waiter, excuse me, I'll have the fricken.
See, that's funny with the fricken, right?
No, it just reminds me of something this guy did today at work.
I told you about that funny guy, Jeffrey, right?
Yeah, he came up.
Well, he did this bit. You probably had to be there...
but it was Liza Minnelli locked in our freezer eating a raw chicken.
Oh, ha, ha.
Were you there? - No, but it sounds fricken funny.
I really understand how hard it's gotta be to leave your child with another person.
I mean, it's like leaving behind a piece of your heart.
Sandy, that's exactly what it is.
Are you gay? - Ross.
It's okay. I get that a lot doing what I do.
But I am straight. I'm engaged, actually. - Oh.
Her name's Delia. - That's pretty.
So you're just, like, a guy who's a nanny.
I realize how it's a bit unorthodox for some people.
But I really believe the most satisfying thing you can do with your life...
is take care of a child.
Okay.
Like at my last job.
I met Daniel when he was 3 weeks old.
And I got to watch him grow into this awesome person.
When I left, I said, "I'll see you soon."
And he said to me, "Skadandy?"
That was his name for me. - Oh, ha, ha.
"I'll see you every day right in..."
It's okay. - Yeah, kids say all kinds of crap.
Oh, God, she must need her diaper changed.
I can take care of that, if you want. - Oh, that would be great.
I love him, I love him, I love him.
Oh, come on. Rach, he's a guy.
So what? He's smart. He's qualified.
Give me one good reason we shouldn't try him out.
Because it's weird.
Why?
What kind of a job is that for a man? A nanny?
I mean, it's like if a woman wanted to be...
Yes?
King?
I, uh, hope you don't mind. I used some of my homemade lotion on Emma.
It's a mixture of calendula and honey cream. It'll dry that rash right up.
Plus, it keeps the hands young.
Yes. Sandy, you're hired.
That's great.
I'm sorry.
It's just such an emotional thing when you're welcomed into a new family.
Oh, God. Come here.
You gotta be at least bi.
Hey.
I need you to set me up for a joke.
When Monica's around, ask me about fire trucks.
Ooh, I don't know, Chandler. I'm not so good with remembering lines.
Well, thank God your livelihood doesn't depend on it.
I know, right?
Why are we doing this?
Monica says that her maitred' is the funniest guy she's ever met.
Seriously? She actually said that?
Yes. Am I crazy to be this upset?
No. Being funny's your thing. - Yeah.
Without that, you just got "lame with women." - Yeah...
Hi. There you are.
Fire trucks.
Wow. You look even more beautiful than you did yesterday.
Ooh. - In fact, I'm going to kiss you now.
Oh, wait, wait. - Yeah, I can't get away with stuff like that.
It sounded sexy in my head, so I...
No, no, it's not that.
Remember when you asked me if I was seeing someone and I said no?
Well, um, I am. His name's Mike. - Oh. Oh.
I should've told you. - No.
Well, yeah. - Yeah.
I'm sorry. I'm sorry. - Well, it's okay. I understand.
Well, are you happy with this guy?
I am happy. - Damn it.
I'm sorry. I don't mean that. I want you to be happy.
But only with me. No, that's not fair. Who cares. Leave him.
I don't mean that. Yes, I do. I'm sorry. Um...
I think I should probably, uh, go. - Well...
But, David, I just want you to know that, you know...
telling you this is one of the hardest things I've ever had to do.
Well, just so you know...
hearing it wasn't exactly a Vladnik carnival, either.
Can we at least hug goodbye? - Of course. Yeah.
You know, and a kiss on the cheek wouldn't be totally inappropriate.
No. No. - I mean...
In Minsk? - Yeah?
It's, um, two on each cheek... - Mm-hm.
and, uh, one on the lips.
Well, if that's what they do in Minsk...
In New York, it's...
Oh, boy.
Hi.
Is everything all right?
Oh, yeah. No, it's fine. It's fine.
Sandy was just telling me about how he proposed to his fiancée...
and it was so beautiful.
Well, her favorite flower is the camellia. From the poem...
I can't hear it again.
You know, I can't tell it again.
And I'm fine never having heard it.
Rach, can I see you for a sec? - Yeah. Excuse me.
Do you realize that man has cried in our apartment three times? Huh?
I haven't cried that many times since I moved in.
Look, Ross, Sandy's just sensitive. That's all.
Okay, okay. See, that is the problem. He is too sensitive.
Too sensitive to take care of our baby?
No, I mean, all I'm saying is that guy... These are amazing.
Sandy made madeleines.
This is exactly what I'm talking about.
What kind of a guy makes delicate French cookies? Huh?
They're not even butch, manly cookies with...
You know, with chunks.
Well, you know, I don't know what to say.
I mean, I never thought of you as a guy who needed his men to be men.
I gotta tell you, Ross, it's not like you just came in from branding cattle.
Hey, there's sensitive and there's too sensitive.
Okay, what is too sensitive?
No, I can't. I can't do this. It's bad.
But it's nice. And nice is good. - Mm-hm.
And good is not bad. Ergo, we should keep kissing.
No, no. No. - But...
Ergo.
Look, David, if you had never left, then...
yeah, we'd probably still be together right now.
But you did leave. And I'm with Mike, and I really care about him.
Well, um, goodbye. Uh...
Well, the key works.
And, you, thanks for the face massage. Thank you.
Did Rachel tell you we hired a male nanny? - Yeah
Yeah. I think that's great. - Oh, really?
Did she tell you he plays the recorder, recites poetry and bakes madeleines?
Oh. How are they? - Lighter than air, but that's not the point.
Hey. - Hey.
Rachel and I hired a male nanny.
Really?
Guys do that?
That's weird. - Thank you.
That's like a woman wanting to be a... - What?
What's the end of that sentence? - Yes. What is the end of that sentence?
Uh...
A penis model.
Anyway, hey, did you tell Chandler that some guy from work...
is the funniest guy you ever met?
Yeah. So? - Wow.
Really? Do you not know Chandler?
Is that why he's acting so weird? He's jealous?
Oh, my God, that is crazy.
It's not like I'm attracted to Jeffrey. JOEY: So what?
Being funny is Chandler's thing. You know, like Ross' thing is...
Science?
Academia? Being a good father? - No.
I can't believe he's that upset about this.
You have to do some damage control.
Because he's feeling like...

I don't know, it's... Well, just the way you say it.
I mean, you're funny. You have that funny thing. You're a funny guy.

Yeah.

Honey, listen.
You have nothing to worry about with Jeffrey.

I mean, you're more sarcastic.

I do limericks.

Yup.

Kiss him? - Oh, well, yeah.
Yes, but you should know, she really likes you.

I can't watch. It's like firing Elmo.
Sandy? Hi.
Hi. - We, uh...
We kind of need to talk.
I'm afraid it's not working out.
Oh. - Yeah, um...
I mean, Rachel and I think you are great with Emma. Um...

I just feel...
that the chemistry isn't right. I'm sorry.

I just picked you guys because...
I liked you the best. - Oh, damn you, Geller.

what was the problem? Maybe it's something I can work on in the future.

Uh, heh...
Please?

with a guy who's as sensitive as you.

Um... Uh...

Mm.
I mean, uh, you know, when I was growing up, he was a tough guy.

I play squash.
Anyway, I, uh... I always got the feeling he thought I was too sensitive.

It was hard.
I remember I was in my bedroom, playing with my dinosaurs...
Playing and learning.
And my father walks in and says, "What are you doing with those things?
What's wrong with you?

What kind? - A friendship.
Wow. You blow my mind.
Oh, I gotta go. - Aw.
How much do I owe you? - Twenty bucks.
It's like the cheapest college ever.

sense_groups.english: Wow. Where's your luggage?

sense_groups.chinese: 该死
sense_groups.english: Damn it.

sense_groups.chinese: 好了 我来打电话给计程车行
sense_groups.english: All right, I'll call the cab company.

sense_groups.chinese: 等等…我们可以等一下再打 你可以先站在那边一下子吗？
sense_groups.english: We can call them later. Can you just stand there for a moment?

sense_groups.chinese: 天啊
sense_groups.english: Boy.

sense_groups.chinese: 有一句俄罗斯老谚语是这样的
sense_groups.english: There's an old Russian expression, um, that goes

sense_groups.chinese: 大略的翻译就是
sense_groups.english: Roughly translated, that means, um

sense_groups.chinese: "我现在盯着的东西 哇"
sense_groups.english: "This thing that I'm looking at: Wow."

sense_groups.chinese: 谢谢你
sense_groups.english: Thank you.

sense_groups.chinese: 你应该看看当我… 事实上 不用 我看起来挺不错的
sense_groups.english: Uh, no, you should see me when... Actually, no, I look pretty good.

sense_groups.chinese: 你在开玩笑吗？
sense_groups.english: Are you kidding?

sense_groups.chinese: 你知道的 当很久没有见到一个人…
sense_groups.english: You know, when you don't see someone for a long time...

sense_groups.chinese: 你会在脑海中建立起这个人的影像 然后开始想
sense_groups.english: and you kind of build them up in your head, you start thinking

sense_groups.chinese: "少来了 别发神经了 没有人是那样美的"
sense_groups.english: "Come on, don't be crazy, nobody's that beautiful."

sense_groups.chinese: 但是 嗯 你真的就是那样的美
sense_groups.english: But, well, you are.

sense_groups.chinese: 那么 你现在有在跟谁交往吗？
sense_groups.english: Well, so, um, are you seeing anyone?

sense_groups.chinese: 没有
sense_groups.english: No.

sense_groups.chinese: 我是最糟糕的人
sense_groups.english: I'm just the worst person ever.

sense_groups.chinese: 我怎么可以不告诉大卫 我跟麦克在一起呢？
sense_groups.english: How can I not tell David that I'm seeing Mike?

sense_groups.chinese: 或许他没有给你机会说
sense_groups.english: Maybe he didn't give you a chance.

sense_groups.chinese: 他问我有没有跟谁交往 而我说没有
sense_groups.english: He said, "Are you seeing someone?" And I said, "No."

sense_groups.chinese: 喔 那本来是你可以澄清的机会的 - 是的
sense_groups.english: Oh, well, that would've been your window. - Yeah.

sense_groups.chinese: 我真的不知道 我看着他的双眼…
sense_groups.english: I mean, I don't know. I was looking in his eyes...

sense_groups.chinese: 然后只能想 我的天 是大卫 大卫在这
sense_groups.english: and I was just thinking, "Oh, my God, it's David. David's here."

sense_groups.chinese: 他真是令人无法抗拒
sense_groups.english: He's just so irresistible.

sense_groups.chinese: 真的吗？那个科学家？ - 真的吗？钱德？
sense_groups.english: Really? The scientist guy? - Really? Chandler?

sense_groups.chinese: 继续说
sense_groups.english: Continue.

sense_groups.chinese: 然后越来越糟糕…
sense_groups.english: Okay, then it gets worse...

sense_groups.chinese: 因为我答应他明晚跟他见面
sense_groups.english: because I told him I would see him tomorrow night.

sense_groups.chinese: 菲比 - 我知道 邪恶的女人
sense_groups.english: Phoebe. - I know. Evil.

sense_groups.chinese: 同时
sense_groups.english: And, and, and, and...

sense_groups.chinese: 我真的好喜欢麦克 你知道吗？发展得真的很顺利 我的天
sense_groups.english: I like Mike so much, you know? It's just going really well. Oh, my God.

sense_groups.chinese: 大卫出现在你跟麦克 交换钥匙的同一天…
sense_groups.english: Wow, isn't it ironic that David would show up...

sense_groups.chinese: 这真是很讽刺是吗？
sense_groups.english: on the same day that you and Mike exchange keys?

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯哈
sense_groups.english: Uh-huh.

sense_groups.chinese: 是啊 而且你知道我一辈子都在 找寻讽刺的事…
sense_groups.english: Yeah. You know, and given my lifelong search for irony...

sense_groups.chinese: 你可以想像得到我有多开心
sense_groups.english: you can imagine how happy I am.

sense_groups.chinese: 你要怎么办呢？ - 我想我只能…
sense_groups.english: What are you gonna do? - I mean, I guess I just have to...

sense_groups.chinese: 告诉大卫我们之间是不可能的
sense_groups.english: tell David that nothing can happen between us.

sense_groups.chinese: 除非我不用告诉他
sense_groups.english: Unless I don't.

sense_groups.chinese: 你知道的 复杂的道德情况…
sense_groups.english: You know, complicated moral situation?

sense_groups.chinese: 是没有错或对 - 你必须要告诉大卫
sense_groups.english: No right, no wrong? - You have to tell David.

sense_groups.chinese: 我就知道我应该去问乔伊才对
sense_groups.english: I knew I should've had this conversation with Joey.

sense_groups.chinese: 她遇过最风趣的男人…
sense_groups.english: Funniest guy she's ever met.

sense_groups.chinese: 我很风趣 不是吗？
sense_groups.english: I'm funny, right?

sense_groups.chinese: 你知道个什么？你只是一道门
sense_groups.english: What do you know? You're a door.

sense_groups.chinese: 你就像是敲敲门笑话
sense_groups.english: You just like knock-knock jokes.

sense_groups.chinese: 等到里面再发挥
sense_groups.english: Save it for inside.

sense_groups.chinese: 嘿 - 嘿
sense_groups.english: Hey. - Hey.

sense_groups.chinese: 奥克拉荷马真是疯狂 他们把那里称为早到者之州
sense_groups.english: So Oklahoma's a crazy place. You know, they call it the Sooner State.

sense_groups.chinese: 事实上 我还真希望 可以早点离开到其他的州
sense_groups.english: Frankly, I'd sooner be in any other state.

sense_groups.chinese: 而且奥克拉荷马 为什么有个平底锅柄呢？
sense_groups.english: And what's with Oklahoma having a panhandle?

sense_groups.chinese: 其他的州可以有像那样的东西吗？
sense_groups.english: Can all states have stuff like that?

sense_groups.chinese: 嘿 我是从怀俄明的中腰部来的
sense_groups.english: Hey, yeah, I'm from the, uh, waistband of Wyoming.

sense_groups.chinese: 但是当我七岁的时候 我们就搬到胯下部了
sense_groups.english: But when I was 7, we headed over to the crotch.

sense_groups.chinese: 你的机舱是不是有加压呢？
sense_groups.english: Was your cabin pressurized?

sense_groups.chinese: 而且不要让我开始告诉你们 土尔沙人说话的方式…
sense_groups.english: And don't get me started on the way the people from Tulsa talk.

sense_groups.chinese: 好的
sense_groups.english: Okay.

sense_groups.chinese: "你全"到底是个什么字呢？
sense_groups.english: What's with the word "y'all"?

sense_groups.chinese: 只不过是"你们"跟"全部"加在一起
sense_groups.english: You know, just two words just pushed together?

sense_groups.chinese: 我们可以那样做吗？因为如果可以 还有很多字可以这样玩
sense_groups.english: Are we all allowed to do that? Because if so, I say why stop there?

sense_groups.chinese: 你的 新狮子狗 可以变成你的新狮
sense_groups.english: You know, your new poodle could be your noodle.

sense_groups.chinese: 油炸鸡块 可以变成 炸块
sense_groups.english: And fried chicken could be fricken.

sense_groups.chinese: 服务生？服务生 不好意思 我想要点 炸块
sense_groups.english: Waiter? Waiter, excuse me, I'll have the fricken.

sense_groups.chinese: 瞧 炸块 很好笑吧？
sense_groups.english: See, that's funny with the fricken, right?

sense_groups.chinese: 不 只是让我想起今天工作时 有个人讲的笑话…
sense_groups.english: No, it just reminds me of something this guy did today at work.

sense_groups.chinese: 我有跟你提过一个风趣的人叫做杰佛瑞 对吗？
sense_groups.english: I told you about that funny guy, Jeffrey, right?

sense_groups.chinese: 是啊 你提过
sense_groups.english: Yeah, he came up.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯 他做了一件事 你应该要在现场才感受得到…
sense_groups.english: Well, he did this bit. You probably had to be there...

sense_groups.chinese: 莉莎明妮莉被锁在冰箱里面吃生鸡肉
sense_groups.english: but it was Liza Minnelli locked in our freezer eating a raw chicken.

sense_groups.chinese: 喔
sense_groups.english: Oh, ha, ha.

sense_groups.chinese: 你在现场吗？ - 没有 但是听起来真是 炸块 好笑
sense_groups.english: Were you there? - No, but it sounds fricken funny.

sense_groups.chinese: 我真的可以理解要把孩子交付给 另一个人是很困难的事
sense_groups.english: I really understand how hard it's gotta be to leave your child with another person.

sense_groups.chinese: 我是说 这就像把心上的一块肉割下
sense_groups.english: I mean, it's like leaving behind a piece of your heart.

sense_groups.chinese: 珊帝 这正是如此
sense_groups.english: Sandy, that's exactly what it is.

sense_groups.chinese: 你是同性恋吗？ - 罗斯
sense_groups.english: Are you gay? - Ross.

sense_groups.chinese: 没关系 我的工作常引来误会
sense_groups.english: It's okay. I get that a lot doing what I do.

sense_groups.chinese: 但我不是同性恋 事实上我已经订婚 - 噢
sense_groups.english: But I am straight. I'm engaged, actually. - Oh.

sense_groups.chinese: 她的名字叫做狄莉亚 - 真是好名字
sense_groups.english: Her name's Delia. - That's pretty.

sense_groups.chinese: 所以你只是一个当保姆的男人
sense_groups.english: So you're just, like, a guy who's a nanny.

sense_groups.chinese: 我知道这对一些人来说是很颠覆传统的
sense_groups.english: I realize how it's a bit unorthodox for some people.

sense_groups.chinese: 但我真的相信照顾小孩是一辈子当中…
sense_groups.english: But I really believe the most satisfying thing you can do with your life...

sense_groups.chinese: 最令人感到满足的事
sense_groups.english: is take care of a child.

sense_groups.chinese: 好吧
sense_groups.english: Okay.

sense_groups.chinese: 就像我上一个工作…
sense_groups.english: Like at my last job.

sense_groups.chinese: 我在丹尼尔三星期大的时候就认识他
sense_groups.english: I met Daniel when he was 3 weeks old.

sense_groups.chinese: 然后我看着他成长变成一个很棒的人
sense_groups.english: And I got to watch him grow into this awesome person.

sense_groups.chinese: 当我离开的时候 我说 希望很快再见到你
sense_groups.english: When I left, I said, "I'll see you soon."

sense_groups.chinese: 然后他说 珊卡丹帝
sense_groups.english: And he said to me, "Skadandy?"

sense_groups.chinese: 那是他给我的名字 - 哦 哈哈
sense_groups.english: That was his name for me. - Oh, ha, ha.

sense_groups.chinese: 我每天都会看到你 就在…
sense_groups.english: "I'll see you every day right in..."

sense_groups.chinese: 没关系 - 是啊 小孩子尽会说些鬼话
sense_groups.english: It's okay. - Yeah, kids say all kinds of crap.

sense_groups.chinese: 喔 天啊 她一定是需要换尿布了
sense_groups.english: Oh, God, she must need her diaper changed.

sense_groups.chinese: 我可以帮你处理 如果你要的话 - 太棒了
sense_groups.english: I can take care of that, if you want. - Oh, that would be great.

sense_groups.chinese: 我爱他 我爱他 我爱他
sense_groups.english: I love him, I love him, I love him.

sense_groups.chinese: 别这样 瑞秋 他是个男人
sense_groups.english: Oh, come on. Rach, he's a guy.

sense_groups.chinese: 那又如何？他很聪明 资历又符合
sense_groups.english: So what? He's smart. He's qualified.

sense_groups.chinese: 给我一个理由为什么我们不能试用他
sense_groups.english: Give me one good reason we shouldn't try him out.

sense_groups.chinese: 因为这实在太奇怪了
sense_groups.english: Because it's weird.

sense_groups.chinese: 为什么？
sense_groups.english: Why?

sense_groups.chinese: 男人做那种工作像话吗？保姆？
sense_groups.english: What kind of a job is that for a man? A nanny?

sense_groups.chinese: 我是说 那就像一个女人想要成为…
sense_groups.english: I mean, it's like if a woman wanted to be...

sense_groups.chinese: 什么？
sense_groups.english: Yes?

sense_groups.chinese: 国王？
sense_groups.english: King?

sense_groups.chinese: 我希望你不介意 我在艾玛身上 用了我自制的乳液
sense_groups.english: I, uh, hope you don't mind. I used some of my homemade lotion on Emma.

sense_groups.chinese: 那是混合金盏花跟峰蜜的乳液 对红疹是立即效果的
sense_groups.english: It's a mixture of calendula and honey cream. It'll dry that rash right up.

sense_groups.chinese: 而且 使双手保持年轻
sense_groups.english: Plus, it keeps the hands young.

sense_groups.chinese: 是的 珊帝 你录取了
sense_groups.english: Yes. Sandy, you're hired.

sense_groups.chinese: 太棒了
sense_groups.english: That's great.

sense_groups.chinese: 不好意思
sense_groups.english: I'm sorry.

sense_groups.chinese: 只是被欢迎加入一个新家庭 是一件很令人感动的事
sense_groups.english: It's just such an emotional thing when you're welcomed into a new family.

sense_groups.chinese: 喔 天啊 过来这里
sense_groups.english: Oh, God. Come here.

sense_groups.chinese: 你至少也是双性恋
sense_groups.english: You gotta be at least bi.

sense_groups.chinese: 嘿
sense_groups.english: Hey.

sense_groups.chinese: 我需要你帮忙 让我讲笑话…
sense_groups.english: I need you to set me up for a joke.

sense_groups.chinese: 当摩妮卡在的时候 问我消防车怎样
sense_groups.english: When Monica's around, ask me about fire trucks.

sense_groups.chinese: 我不知道 钱德 我不是很会记台词的
sense_groups.english: Ooh, I don't know, Chandler. I'm not so good with remembering lines.

sense_groups.chinese: 感谢上帝你不是靠记台词吃饭的
sense_groups.english: Well, thank God your livelihood doesn't depend on it.

sense_groups.chinese: 我知道 棒吧？
sense_groups.english: I know, right?

sense_groups.chinese: 我们为什么要这样做呢？
sense_groups.english: Why are we doing this?

sense_groups.chinese: 摩妮卡说他们餐厅的领班 是她遇过最风趣的男人
sense_groups.english: Monica says that her maitred' is the funniest guy she's ever met.

sense_groups.chinese: 真的吗？她真的那样说？
sense_groups.english: Seriously? She actually said that?

sense_groups.chinese: 是的 我这么不爽很疯狂吗？
sense_groups.english: Yes. Am I crazy to be this upset?

sense_groups.chinese: 不 风趣是你的专利 - 是啊
sense_groups.english: No. Being funny's your thing. - Yeah.

sense_groups.chinese: 没有了它 你还有什么吸引女人的 - 对…
sense_groups.english: Without that, you just got "lame with women." - Yeah...

sense_groups.chinese: 嗨 你们都在
sense_groups.english: Hi. There you are.

sense_groups.chinese: 消防车
sense_groups.english: Fire trucks.

sense_groups.chinese: 哇 你看起来比昨天更美丽
sense_groups.english: Wow. You look even more beautiful than you did yesterday.

sense_groups.chinese: 噢 - 事实上 我现在要亲你
sense_groups.english: Ooh. - In fact, I'm going to kiss you now.

sense_groups.chinese: 等等… - 我就是没有办法…
sense_groups.english: Oh, wait, wait. - Yeah, I can't get away with stuff like that.

sense_groups.chinese: 在我脑海中听起来很性感 所以我…
sense_groups.english: It sounded sexy in my head, so I...

sense_groups.chinese: 不 不 不是那件事
sense_groups.english: No, no, it's not that.

sense_groups.chinese: 你记得当你问我有没有跟谁交往 而我告诉你没有吗？
sense_groups.english: Remember when you asked me if I was seeing someone and I said no?

sense_groups.chinese: 事实上我有 他叫做麦克 喔… - 喔…
sense_groups.english: Well, um, I am. His name's Mike. - Oh. Oh.

sense_groups.chinese: 我应该早点告诉你的 - 不用…
sense_groups.english: I should've told you. - No.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯 你应该要的 - 耶
sense_groups.english: Well, yeah. - Yeah.

sense_groups.chinese: 我很抱歉 我很抱歉 - 没关系 我可以理解
sense_groups.english: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. - Well, it's okay. I understand.

sense_groups.chinese: 那 你跟这个人在一起快乐吗？
sense_groups.english: Well, are you happy with this guy?

sense_groups.chinese: 我是很快乐 - 该死
sense_groups.english: I am happy. - Damn it.

sense_groups.chinese: 我很抱歉 我不是那个意思 我要你过得快乐
sense_groups.english: I'm sorry. I don't mean that. I want you to be happy.

sense_groups.chinese: 但是只能跟我 不 那并不公平 管他的 抛弃他吧
sense_groups.english: But only with me. No, that's not fair. Who cares. Leave him.

sense_groups.chinese: 我不是那个意思 是的 我是 我很抱歉
sense_groups.english: I don't mean that. Yes, I do. I'm sorry. Um...

sense_groups.chinese: 我想我应该离开了 - 好吧...
sense_groups.english: I think I should probably, uh, go. - Well...

sense_groups.chinese: 但是 大卫 我只想要你知道…
sense_groups.english: But, David, I just want you to know that, you know...

sense_groups.chinese: 跟你坦白 是我做过最困难的事
sense_groups.english: telling you this is one of the hardest things I've ever had to do.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯 让你知道一下…
sense_groups.english: Well, just so you know...

sense_groups.chinese: 听到这件事也不是像在过嘉年华
sense_groups.english: hearing it wasn't exactly a Vladnik carnival, either.

sense_groups.chinese: 我们至少可以拥抱道别吧？ - 当然 可以
sense_groups.english: Can we at least hug goodbye? - Of course. Yeah.

sense_groups.chinese: 你知道的 在脸颊上亲一下 应该不会是太不适当
sense_groups.english: You know, and a kiss on the cheek wouldn't be totally inappropriate.

sense_groups.chinese: 不 不 - 我是说…
sense_groups.english: No. No. - I mean...

sense_groups.chinese: 在明斯克… - 怎样呢？
sense_groups.english: In Minsk? - Yeah?

sense_groups.chinese: 是在两边各亲两下… - 嗯
sense_groups.english: It's, um, two on each cheek... - Mm-hm.

sense_groups.chinese: 还有一下亲在唇上
sense_groups.english: and, uh, one on the lips.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯 好吧 如果那是明斯克的习俗
sense_groups.english: Well, if that's what they do in Minsk...

sense_groups.chinese: 在纽约 是…
sense_groups.english: In New York, it's...

sense_groups.chinese: 喔 天啊
sense_groups.english: Oh, boy.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗨
sense_groups.english: Hi.

sense_groups.chinese: 一切都还好吧？
sense_groups.english: Is everything all right?

sense_groups.chinese: 喔 是的 很好 很好
sense_groups.english: Oh, yeah. No, it's fine. It's fine.

sense_groups.chinese: 珊帝只是在告诉我他是如何 跟他未婚妻求婚的…
sense_groups.english: Sandy was just telling me about how he proposed to his fiancée...

sense_groups.chinese: 实在是太梦幻了
sense_groups.english: and it was so beautiful.

sense_groups.chinese: 她最喜欢的花是山茶花 从那首诗…
sense_groups.english: Well, her favorite flower is the camellia. From the poem...

sense_groups.chinese: 我没办法再听一次
sense_groups.english: I can't hear it again.

sense_groups.chinese: 我也没办法再说一次
sense_groups.english: You know, I can't tell it again.

sense_groups.chinese: 而我也还好不用听到
sense_groups.english: And I'm fine never having heard it.

sense_groups.chinese: 瑞秋 我可以跟你说一下话吗？ - 好啊 失陪了
sense_groups.english: Rach, can I see you for a sec? - Yeah. Excuse me.

sense_groups.chinese: 你有发现那男人在我们家 已经哭过三次了吗？
sense_groups.english: Do you realize that man has cried in our apartment three times? Huh?

sense_groups.chinese: 我从搬进来之后也没哭过那么多次
sense_groups.english: I haven't cried that many times since I moved in.

sense_groups.chinese: 听着 罗斯 珊帝只不过是很敏感 不过是如此
sense_groups.english: Look, Ross, Sandy's just sensitive. That's all.

sense_groups.chinese: 好了 看吧 那就是个问题 他太敏感了
sense_groups.english: Okay, okay. See, that is the problem. He is too sensitive.

sense_groups.chinese: 太敏感就不能照顾我们的小孩吗？
sense_groups.english: Too sensitive to take care of our baby?

sense_groups.chinese: 不 我是说 那个男的… 这真是太好吃了
sense_groups.english: No, I mean, all I'm saying is that guy... These are amazing.

sense_groups.chinese: 珊帝做的马德琳饼干
sense_groups.english: Sandy made madeleines.

sense_groups.chinese: 这就正是我在说的

questions.en:
Hey, hon? Would you help me get the plates down?
Hey, here's an idea. Why don't we use our wedding china today?
No, I think we should save our china for something really special.
Like if the queen of England comes over.
Honey, she keeps canceling on us. Take the hint.
What if something breaks? They're expensive.
What is the point of having them if we never use them?
Okay. But if something breaks and then the queen comes over...
I will explain it to her. - Like I'd let you talk to the queen.
The parade is really good this year.
Man, those horses can crap.
Next up is a marching band from Muskogee, Oklahoma.
Muskogee? That's like four hours from Tulsa!
Here's the float with the stars of the popular daytime soap...
Days of our Lives.
Oh, my God!
Aren't you one of the stars of the popular daytime soap Days ofour Lives?
I forgot! I'm supposed to be there!
I can't believe I forgot! I usually write stuff like this down on my arm!
Stupid long sleeves!
What are you gonna do? - I'll come up with a good reason...
why I wasn't there.
The producers are gonna be mad. They sat us down and said
"Everyone has to be there, 6 a.m. Sharp. That means you, Tribbiani."
Like I was some kind of idiot.
Well, you proved them wrong. - Yeah.
Oh, Emma.
This is your first Thanksgiving.
What are you thankful for?
Mommy's boobies?
A lot of people are thankful for those.
Hello? Rachel?
Who is it?
It's your favorite sister.
Jill? - Amy!
Hide my rings.
Amy! Happy Thanksgiving.
Do you have a hair straightener?
Um... Hi.
Hi. - Hi.Hair straightener.
I haven't seen you in, like, a year. - I know. I've just been crazed.
Well, me too. I had a baby.
I decorated Dad's office.
Yeah? Well, unless you pushed a desk out of your vagina, not the same thing.
About that hair straightener, honey, I really need one.
I'm gonna have dinner at my boyfriend's house.
Oh, my God. - Uh-huh.
Is this Emmett?
It's Emma.
It's a girl?
Hey, Amy. - Amy, you remember Ross?
Not really.
But you are much cuter than that geeky guy she used to date.
That was me.
No, he was this creepy guy from high school who had this huge crush on her...
since, like, the ninth grade.
Still me.
No, I'm not talking about you.
It was your fat friend's brother with that bad Afro.
Okay, Amy, I'm gonna save you some time, okay? All me!
Careful. Careful.
Careful!
I'll tell you what. For the rest of our lives...
I'll be careful until told otherwise.
This isn't the china we picked out. MONICA: I know.
After you left the store, I chose different ones.
Why? - Your taste is a little feminine for me.
Suddenly flowers are feminine?
Hey, everybody! Happy Thanksgiving!
Happy Thanksgiving. Pheebs! - What's going on, Joe?
Listen, I need a good lie.
Okay.
How about the whole "man walking on the moon" thing, you know?
You can see the strings, people!
No, no, no. I need a good lie to explain why I wasn't at a work thing today.
Honey, you stink at lying. - I do not.
Really? Let me ask you something. Yesterday at the coffeehouse...
I went to the bathroom. When I came back, my muffin was gone. Who took it?
Somebody opened the door to the coffeehouse...
and a raccoon ran in and went straight for your muffin. I said
"Hey, don't eat that! That's Phoebe's!" And he said...
He said, "Joey, you stink at lying." What am I gonna do?
Don't worry. We'll come up with a lie. I'll help you.
Great. That'd be great. Thank you. - Sure. What was the work thing?
Uh...
"Pick up Grandma at the airport." - Oh, man!
She's precious.
Do you ever worry that she's gonna get your real nose?
Amy...
Yes, I do. I really do.
Hello?
Yeah, hang on, one sec. Can I take this upstairs?
Sure. We don't live there, but...
Seriously? It's just these rooms?
I thought you were a doctor. - Yeah. No, Ross has a Ph.D.
Ew!
God, she is unbelievable.
I know. I mean, a Ph.D. Is just as good as an MD.
Sure, Ross, yeah!
If I have a heart attack at a restaurant, I want you there with your fossil brush.
Stupid Thanksgiving. - What?
What? What happened? - My boyfriend canceled on me.
I mean, I finally find a real relationship.
Someone that I can spend this day with, and then his wife comes back into town!
I swear, it's almost not even worth dating married guys.
Don't say that.
God, I was so looking forward to this.
It was gonna be such a beautiful Thanksgiving.
We were gonna have sushi.
Amy, don't cry.
Ross, can I talk to you in private?
Sure, you wanna go upstairs, or?
Look, I was thinking, if it's okay with Monica...
I would like to invite Amy to Thanksgiving.
I think that's a great idea. It'll be like the Pilgrims
bringing the Indians syphilis.
Look, I know she's a little tough to take.
But she has nowhere else to go, and she's my sister. She's Emma's aunt.
And I would like them to bond. - I don't want them bonding too much.
I don't want her telling Emma she needs a nose job.
Ross, she may need one. We're just gonna have to make our peace with that!
Hi! - Hey.
Hey, you guys. This is my sister Amy.
This is Chandler, Joey, Phoebe, and you know Mon.
Hi. - Oh, my God.
You're on Days of our Lives!
Yeah.
Wow! They must put a lot of makeup on you.
Happy Thanksgiving.
Hey - Hi.
So welcome. Is this the first time you're seeing Emma?
Yeah, I think so. It's nice to meet you, Emma.
Phoebe. - That's a funny noise.
Pheebs? I still need some help here. - Right. Okay.
So it's not just the lie you tell, but it's the way you tell it. For example...
if you look at the ground when you talk, people know you're lying.
I don't know why this is so hard for me. Lying is basically just acting...
and I am a terrific actor. - You are a terrific actor.
Hey. Where's the baby? - We just put her down for a nap.
Listen, I was just thinking. You know what would be incredible?
If you guys died!
Thank you, Amy.
No, no, then I would get the baby.
It would be just like a movie. At first I wouldn't know what to do with her.
And then I would rise to the occasion. Then I'd get a makeover and get married.
That's a great movie!
Yeah. Listen, not that you guys could stop me or anything...
because, you know, you'd be dead.
But I was thinking about changing her name.
I'm just not really a big fan of Emily.
Emma.
Emma? Ross wants you.
Phoebe!
Why does she keep making that noise?
Honey, I don't know how to tell you this...
but if something were to happen to Ross or myself...
you wouldn't get the baby. - Well, who would?
Well, we haven't officially asked them yet...
but we would want Monica and Chandler.
I can't believe you'd want us to raise Emma.
Oh, my God, I'm so moved.
I don't believe this. Hold on a second. You guys die...
and I don't get your baby?
Amy, see, we're a lot closer to Monica and Chandler.
We see them every day. And truthfully, you don't seem connected to the baby.
Connected? To what? She's a lump.
You know, guys, I've gotta say this means so much to me.
I mean, that you would trust me with your child.
I mean, we all know that Monica and I have been...
trying to have a baby of our own.
You know, I've had my doubts about my skills as a father, but...
That you two...
That you two... - This guy?
Seriously?
Okay, it's time for dinner.
Everyone, we're using our fancy china...
and it's very expensive, so please be careful.
Whoa. Whoa. Whoa...
Okay, just to be clear, comedy with the plates will not be well-received.
Hey!
How come my plate's less fancy than everyone else's?
Do you not trust me with a fancy plate?
No, honey. That's a special plate.
See, it's a game. Whoever gets that plate wins.
I can't believe I won!
You know, this is such a slap in the face. I mean, I'm your sister...
and you would give your baby to these strangers over me.
Monica is Ross' sister.
No, Ross' sister was really fat.
That was me.
No, she was this dorky girl in school who followed Rachel around like a puppy...
Amy, you've got to stop doing that!
Okay, listen, I know you're having a bit of a family crisis...
but you don't have to take it out on the plates.
I mean, in fact, I think that everyone...
should cut their food like this
Now, see? This way, you protect the plates...
and let's face it, you have fun.
Okay, how about this? If you guys die...
and the crazy plate lady dies...
then do I get the baby? - No, if crazy plate lady...
If Monica dies, then I would get Emma. Right?
Well, actually... - Actually what?
It's just... It's just that in that case...
then Emma would go to my parents.
What? - Hurts, doesn't it?
Who has to die for me to get her?
So if Monica's not around, I'm not good enough to raise Emma?
No, that is not what we're saying.
Yeah, he's lying. He looked down.
Well, what's wrong with me? Am I incompetent?
Because I managed to survive whatever it is that killed the three of you!
You're taking this the wrong way. We think you'll be a wonderful parent.
It's just... You're more the, you know, fun parent.
Yeah, and we wanna make sure Emma also has someone like Monica...
who's more of a disciplinarian.
Someone who can be firm and strict.
That's not how you see me, is it?
No, you're all about the fun.
I may not know a lot about babies, but do you really think I'm not capable?
No. You both are equally capable.
It's just you're strongest when you're together.
Okay. So if we both had Emma, and I died...
she'd have to give her up.
Sure. Monica would have to give her up.
I lie better than that, right?
Let me just get this straight. So my two friends die, I get Emma.
Then my wife dies. Then Emma, the one tiny ray of hope left in my life...
gets taken away from me? - There's your movie.
Hey, there you are.
You disappeared after dinner. - Did somebody miss me?
Was there a child to raise poorly?
Ross and Rachel don't know what they're saying.
It's not like they're so responsible.
Emma is a product of a bottle of merlot and a five-year-old condom.
No, but they're right. I'm not a strong father figure, and I never will be.
No, you learn these things. You grow into it.
Yeah, but it's not who I am.
Everything they said is exactly why I was worried about having a kid. And it's true.
And look, everybody knows it. - I don't know it.
I wanna have a kid with you because I think you'll be an amazing dad.
At the fun parts and at the hard parts.
Well, can you picture me saying, "Go to your room, you're grounded"?
Can you hear me say, "You're grounded"?
You said that to me last week.
How hard is it? "No shoes on the furniture!"
The producer from Days left a message asking why I wasn't at the parade.
They said everybody's really pissed off at me. And they all got to meet Santa!
It's okay. I thought of the perfect lie for you.
It's easy to remember, and it doesn't invite a lot of questions.
You weren't at the parade, because you had a family emergency.
I like that! Yeah!
I wasn't at the parade, because I had a family emergency.
What happened?
My sister's raccoon came... - No, nothing with a raccoon!
Wait, what are you doing? - Setting the table.
We thought it might be nice to use the fancy china for dessert too.
How nice. Maybe later we can all blow our noses on my wedding dress.
Hey, dude, you okay? Sorry about before.
That's okay. You're totally right. I don't know anything about disciplining a child.
But it did hurt my feelings, and I want you to know that if I die...
you don't get Joey.
In case you hadn't noticed, I'm not talking to you.
You know, this is just... This is classic Rachel.
Right. Remember in high school when I died and didn't give you my baby?
This might be my one chance to have a child, Rachel.
I mean, you know that I have been so busy focusing on my career...
What career? - I'm a decorator.
You decorate Dad's office and now you're a decorator?
Okay, I went to the zoo yesterday, now I'm a koala bear.
Why can't you ever be supportive? - You want to talk supportive?
You didn't come and visit me when I was in the hospital having the baby!
You didn't come see me in the hospital when I was getting my lips done!
I did the first time.
You know what? You want to know why I am not giving Emily to you?
Emma. - Whose side are you on?!
I'm not giving you Emma, because you can't handle the responsibility of a child.
Well, how hard could it be? You do it.
Ooh-hoo-hoo-hoo.
You wanna know why you don't want me to have the baby?
Because you don't want me to be happy.
You have always been jealous of me. - Jealous of what?
Of your lack of responsibility? Your immaturity?
Your total disregard for other people's feelings?
To name a few.
You've always been like this.
You had to have everything, and I couldn't have anything.
Like in junior high, when you stole Timmy from me.
I mean, do you even realize how much that hurt me?
Timmy was my boyfriend, and you made out with him!
Come on, that was 20 years ago. Get over it.
I cannot believe that I invited you here today!
Yeah, well, you know what I cannot believe? That my so-called sister...
gets a 30% discount from Ralph Lauren, and I still have to pay retail?
It's 45.
You bitch.
You just think you're so perfect...
with your new baby and your small apartment.
Well, let me tell you something. Your baby isn't even that cute.
Too far, Amy. Too far.
You take that back. - No.
Take it back! - No. What are you gonna do? Make me?
Hey, man, I work out!
So do I. - I do Pilates.
I do yoga. - Bring it on!
Put the plates in the boxes! Put the plates in the boxes!
Did you just push me? - Yeah, I think I did.
All right, that's it.
Forget the bubble wrap! There isn't time!
Frizzy, frizzy, frizzy!
Shouldn't we stop this? - Are you out of your mind?
Let's throw some Jell-O on them!
Gross!
All right, that is it! This is our apartment, and you cannot behave this way!
If you can't act your age, you shouldn't be here at all.
Those plates may not be as nice as the pretty pink ones that I picked out...
but they're important to Monica. And I want you to apologize to her now.
I'm sorry. - Mon, I'm so sorry.
Okay. That's better.
Now, I want you to apologize to each other and mean it.
Sorry. - Sorry.
By the way, that fight was totally arousing.
Dude, well done.
If I die and Rachel dies and Monica dies, you can totally take care of Emma.
Yeah? Well, thanks.
So... So now do I get Joey?
Okay. But you should know he eats a lot and shoves pennies up his nose.
Are you okay, Mon? - Uh-huh.
I mean, these things happen. I mean, it's just a plate.
It's not like somebody died. - It's all right. You can mourn.
Thank you. It was so beautiful!
I'm gonna go to Joey's and get the pies.
Actually, not pies. It's just pie.
I don't care.
Oh, my God, I've lost the will to scold.
Look, Amy...
we got a little...
a little out-of-control over there.
And I'm sorry.
You're my sister...
and if it really means that much to you...
So you're gonna give me the baby? - No, I was...
I was gonna let you use my Ralph Lauren discount.
You are not gonna regret this.
She needs changing. - No, no, no. I'll get her.
I am super confident, totally responsible and fourth in line to raise Emma.
I'll be right there, Emma! Just let me get my trusty diaper bag here.
Well, what do you know? I guess I'll be the one who dies first.
Does Monica know about her plates? CHANDLER: Nope.
Broke them all, huh? - Yep.
You gonna tell her? - Nope.
Hey. So I'm gonna put the plates back.
I think you're right. We shouldn't use these plates for a long time.
Like only if the queen comes? - Maybe not even then.
Hey. I did it.
I told my producer I had a family emergency. He totally bought it.
Thanks for teaching me how to lie. - No problem. Next week, stealing.
Bye, plates. - You told her you broke all the plates?
What?! Something happened with the plates?
Yeah, this raccoon came in...
